Resolves #21702

The time-axis header keeps its look under the pointer. `Neo.timeline.TimeAxisHeader` carries `neo-grid-header-button` for the header toolbar's layout, so the hover `grid/header/Button.css` gives every header button painted the whole scale in the hover colour, with a pointer cursor. `resources/css/src/timeline/TimeAxisHeader.css` now sets `cursor: default` and a `:hover` that restores the rest background, borders, seams and shadow. The structural class stays.

Evidence: L3 (headless Chromium e2e: the header's pixels at rest and hovered, `dev`'s CSS vs head's, five themes) → L3 required (a hover look). Residual: none.

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 no background, border or shadow change on hover in `gantt/basic`, `scheduler/basic`, `timeline/basic`, five themes | CI: `TimeAxisHeaderHover.spec.mjs`, one test per example, each over the five themes (header pixels at rest vs hovered) |
| AC-2 `cursor: default` | CI: the same tests read the computed cursor |
| AC-3 red on `dev`, green at head; `build-themes` and `check-theme-surfaces` pass | Outside CI: Test Evidence below |
| AC-4 before/after whole-page frames of `gantt/basic` hovered in `neo-theme-neo-light` | Test Evidence below |

### 🔬 Depth Floor

- **Challenge**: Non-blocking CSS value-type subtlety in `resources/css/src/timeline/TimeAxisHeader.css:29` — at rest (line `5`), `.neo-timeline-header.neo-grid-header-button` declares `background: var(--neo-timeline-header-background)`, whereas `&:hover` (line `29`) declares `background-color: var(--neo-timeline-header-background)`. In `resources/css/theme-dark/timeline/TimeAxisHeader.css:2`, `--neo-timeline-header-background` resolves to `var(--grid-header-button-background-image, linear-gradient(#3c3f41, #323232))`. Substituting a `<gradient>` into `background-color` is invalid at computed-value time (IACVT), resetting `background-color` on `:hover` to `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` rather than `Button.css:49`'s `--grid-header-button-background-color-hover`, while the rest rule's opaque `linear-gradient(#3c3f41, #323232)` remains in `background-image` (`TimeAxisHeaderHover.spec.mjs` confirms zero pixel delta in `neo-theme-dark`). Using the `background` shorthand on `&:hover` (and mirroring `Button.css:28-30`'s `&.neo-locked-start:last-child` if a timeline column is ever docked `locked: 'start'`) would avoid relying on IACVT if a future theme uses a semi-transparent gradient over a base fill.
